incident-bot: Pager: p99 latency alert for api-redwood-text (hosted) — breached 1500ms threshold (observed p99 = 1784ms) · source=canary-deploy · chan=prod-us-west

luca (oncall): seeing spike on the canary lane, getting pages. Anyone on the rollout?

maya: I kicked the canary earlier this morning (v2.3.0-quant). Traffic at 10% now. Noticed a small uptick during smoke but assumed transient.

devon: pulling the dashboards — p95 jumped from ~220ms to 560ms, p99 up to 1.8s. Streaming sessions show stalls: many keepalive retransmits.

samira: logs show `kv-cache` miss rate spiking and GPU utilization on canary nodes is low. Weird. Uploading a snippet.

samira: ```
[2026-07-02T14:22:10Z] model=v2.3.0-quant request_id=abc123 latency=1784ms kv_cache_hit=false batch_size=1 gpu_util=18%
[2026-07-02T14:22:12Z] model=v2.3.0-quant request_id=abc124 latency=1652ms kv_cache_hit=false batch_size=1 gpu_util=12%
```

luca (oncall): low GPU util + high latency + kv cache misses suggests model variant might not be compatible with current caching strategy. Could be a changed KV format or tokenizer behavior.

deploy-bot: Canary traffic ramp: v2.3.0-quant -> 10% at 14:00 UTC by maya

maya: I didn't change tokenizer, only enabled 4-bit quant and a custom kernel. Could the kernel fall back to CPU for small batches?

devon: checking runtime logs for kernel selection...

devon: ```
runtime: selected_kernel=gpu_opt_v1
runtime: fallback=cpu_dispatcher for attention_kernel on seq_len<64
runtime: note: kernel compiled with compute_cap=8.0, node reports 7.5
```

samira: that compute cap mismatch would cause slower paths. Also kv-cache serialization changed in the model repo (there's a recent PR). If cache keys differ, cache hits go to zero and we re-run longer contexts.

luca (oncall): Customer impact? Any paying customers hitting this canary path?

tess (support): Support queue: two customers reported degraded interactive chat responses (long timeouts) in the last 30m. One on us-west. They're on hosted. Severity: potential P1 if widespread.

luca (oncall): Immediate mitigations: 1) Pause canary ramp 2) Shift canary traffic back to stable variant (v2.2.5) 3) If traffic mix doesn't recover, initiate rollback of canary

maya: I paused the ramp and set canary to 0% traffic. Command I ran: ```redwoodctl rollout set --model v2.3.0-quant --canary 0```

deploy-bot: Canary traffic set to 0% for v2.3.0-quant at 14:25 UTC by maya

devon: rolling metrics now — p99 dropped from 1784ms -> 420ms within 60s. p95 back to ~230ms. Streaming stalls count decreasing.

samira: good sign. But we need to confirm root cause before re-trying. I captured a heap of runtime traces and a diff of tokenizer/kv changes.

luca (oncall): For now, leave rollout paused. Notify customer success for impacted customers and offer mitigation notes.

tess (support): Notifying the two affected accounts with a brief: "We're aware of increased latency in us-west during a canary model rollout; traffic has been paused and serving reverted to stable. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for re-deployment." Will paste CIDs here when done.

maya: quick note — I can roll forward with v2.3 but build a canary with the older KV-serialization to test compatibility. Might take ~45m to rebuild.

devon: also recommend we run a small A/B with headroom: smaller batch sizes, energized runtime kernel selection flags disabled so it uses the conservative kernel. That will isolate kernel vs kv issues.

samira: to reproduce locally: set `KV_SERIALIZATION_VERSION=legacy` and force `--kernel-mode conservative`. I have a repro script.

luca (oncall): Action items (live):
- [x] Pause canary ramp (maya)
- [x] Shift traffic to stable (deploy-bot)
- [x] Notify support (tess)
- [ ] Rebuild canary with legacy-kv (maya)
- [ ] Run A/B with conservative kernel (devon)
- [ ] Postmortem owner assignment (tbd)

devon: after rollback, we should still look at node telemetry — some canary nodes showed low GPU util which suggests config mismatch (compute capability flags or driver mismatch).

samira: collected driver versions: canary nodes had driver 525.x, stable nodes 530.x. That could explain kernel mismatch. I'll add to the incident notes.

luca (oncall): OK. If metrics remain stable for 15m, stand down page and create incident ticket in postmortems.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> degraded -> under-investigation. Alerts suppressed for this thread until 14:45 UTC.

tess (support): Customer updates sent for both accounts. One asked if there was a workaround — recommended switching to stable model id (v2.2.5) via the model param in API. They acknowledged.

maya: I'll start the rebuild with legacy-kv and force kernel compatibility check. ETA 45-60m.

devon: I'll prepare a small canary runbook: 1) repro in staging with mixed tokenizer/kv flags 2) monitor p95/p99 and streaming stall metrics 3) only increase canary when p99 < 400ms for 30m

luca (oncall): Thanks all. I'll take postmortem ownership unless someone volunteers. We'll capture timeline, root causes (driver mismatch + kv-serialization change + kernel fallback), and remediation (CI guardrails for KV versioning, driver compatibility tests, conservative canary ramps).

samira: saving traces and attaching to incident ticket.

incident-bot: Closing note: pages cleared at 14:31 UTC, monitoring window active until 14:46 UTC.

luca (oncall): Stand down in 15 unless regressions. We'll reconvene in #incidents if anything pops.

(14:46 UTC follow-up)

devon: 15m post-mitigation: p95=210ms, p99=390ms, streaming stalls back to baseline. Marking as resolved for now.

luca (oncall): resolving thread. Postmortem ticket: PM-9876 assigned to luca/maya/samira/devon.
